scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Area 2 routes disappeared from r1's RIB after a maintenance
touch on r8. r4 still has its area-1 virtual-link configured.
r8 reports OSPF is running. What's wrong on r8's side?

injection.action: remove the area 1 virtual-link toward r4

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r8 OSPF virtual-link to r4
Mechanism: Virtual-links are two-ended — both routers must
  configure the link, each pointing at the other's router-id.
  r4 has `area 1 virtual-link 18.1.4.1` (pointing at r8).
  r8 had `area 1 virtual-link 14.1.4.1` (pointing at r4).
  When r8's side is removed, the virtual adjacency drops.
  Area 2 (which r8 hosts) becomes disconnected from the
  backbone — its prefixes (18.x loopbacks and 80.0.0.0/8)
  withdraw from everyone.
Localization: r8
Root cause: virtual-link configuration missing on r8
Fix: `vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "area 1 virtual-link 14.1.4.1"`
  on r8

agent.diagnosis_text:
The affected component is OSPF ABR/backbone connectivity on r8 — specifically the virtual-link that should tie area 1 to the backbone (area 0). Mechanism: FRR will not treat a router as an ABR or flood inter-area summaries unless it has an active adjacency to the backbone (real or via virtual-link). With no backbone adjacency, r8 suppresses type-3 LSAs for its area 2 prefixes, so downstream routers (e.g., r1) lose area 2 routes from their RIBs.

Localization: On r8, “show running-config” under router ospf lacks any “area 1 virtual-link …” stanza, and “show ip ospf” reports Area 0 with Total: 0, Active: 0 interfaces and “Number of full virtual adjacencies going through this area: 0.” Meanwhile, r8 has area 1 adjacency to r5 (Full/BDR on 58.1.1.2), proving OSPF is running, and r4 still has “area 1 virtual-link 18.1.4.1” configured. On r4, the OSPF neighbor list shows no virtual-link neighbor, confirming the virtual-link is down from r8’s side.

Root cause: The area 1 virtual-link toward r4 (router-id 14.1.4.1) was removed from r8 during maintenance, leaving r8 without a backbone adjacency.

Corrective fix: Reconfigure r8 to restore the virtual-link: under router ospf add “area 1 virtual-link 14.1.4.1” (router-id of r4). After the VL forms (seen under area 0 neighbors), r8 will resume ABR function and re-originate area 2 summaries, restoring area 2 routes on r1. Alternatively, provide a real area 0 interface.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly localizes the fault to r8, citing missing virtual-link configuration and r8-specific show output.
The report explicitly names the affected component as the OSPF virtual-link tying area 1 to the backbone on r8.

The writeup shows r4 still had the virtual-link while r8 lacked it and explicitly ties the adjacency loss to r8’s one-sided removal, demonstrating that the virtual-link must be configured on both routers (each pointing at the other's router-id).
The agent explicitly recommends adding the area 1 virtual-link on r8 (area 1 virtual-link 14.1.4.1), which matches the expected fix and will restore the backbone adjacency/ABR function.

The agent collected OSPF process and neighbor outputs from r8 (showing router-id and a Full neighbor to r5) and inspected running-configs; the conclusion (missing virtual-link on r8 causing loss of backbone adjacency and area-2 prefixes) follows OSPF logic.
